bullets.text: Underwriting profit margin was 8.5% versus 4% goal; net income rose to $313.7M ($4.11/share) from $250.5M ($3.24/share); operating income $309.1M; ROE reached 20.5% compared to 19.6% in 1995.
Companywide NPW +18% to $3,441.7M; core business NPW +19% to $3,367.2M, representing 98% of total; standard and preferred risks accounted for 10% to 15% of 1996 premium volume.
Underwriting expenses dropped 1.4 pts to 21.6% of premiums, down from 23.0% in 1995 and 35.0% in 1990; steady cost reduction continues to be critical to strategy.

Portfolio grew to $4,450.6M; taxable equivalent total return 7.8%; debt-to-capital 32%; issued $100M notes, redeemed preferred shares for $82.1M, repurchased 1.0M common shares at $41.73 average cost; NPW-to-surplus 2.7:1.
Private passenger auto premium growth believed to make PGR 6th largest U.S. auto insurer; gained share in $22B nonstandard market and continued expanding in $85B standard and preferred market.
Expanded complete program from 37 to 43 states; used TV commercials and direct mail urging consumers to call 1 800 AUTO PRO for PGR quotes and up to three competitor comparison rates.

Reorganized into less hierarchical structure, eliminating COO role and forming an 11-member Policy Team; subdivided into 38 local business units, up from 16 in 1995, emphasizing TQM and process management.

Gainsharing generated 10.8% of total compensation; adjusted 1997 program to credit estimated value from adding new customers, with Policy Team targets at 100%–135% and general managers at 50%–100% of base salary.

Distributed through over 30,000 independent agencies as primary method, joint national accounts, and direct phone; standard and preferred lines helped independent agents match consumer needs and regain lost market share.

Assessing homeowners insurance demand in 1997 to satisfy customer needs, addressing catastrophe risk and single-carrier preference; diversified businesses produced $117.7M revenue and $24.3M pretax profit; acquired 50.1% of auto inspection company.
